gloss: wind direction; trend; way things are going

definitions.explanation: The direction from which the wind is blowing.

definitions.gloss: trend; way things are going; mood
definitions.explanation: The general direction of a situation, attitude, or trend. Used figuratively to describe shifting circumstances or public opinion.

examples.japanese: {風向|かざむ}きが{変|か}わった。
{風向|かざむ}きを{見|み}て{帆|ほ}を{調整|ちょうせい}する。
examples.english: Adjust the sails based on the wind direction.

examples.japanese: {午後|ごご}から{風向|かざむ}きが{北|きた}に{変|か}わり、{急|きゅう}に{寒|さむ}くなった。
examples.english: In the afternoon, the wind shifted to the north and it suddenly got cold.

examples.japanese: {世論|よろん}の{風向|かざむ}きが{変|か}わりつつある。
{上司|じょうし}の{風向|かざむ}きを{見|み}て{発言|はつげん}する。
examples.english: Speak up after reading the boss's mood.

examples.japanese: {選挙|せんきょ}が{近|ちか}づくにつれて{政治|せいじ}の{風向|かざむ}きが{大|おお}きく{変|か}わった。
examples.english: As the election approached, the political winds shifted dramatically.

notes:
Compound of {風|かぜ} (wind) + {向|む}き (direction). The reading {風|かざ} uses the older combining form.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風向|かざむ}きが{変|か}わる (the wind/trend changes)
- {風向|かざむ}きを{見|み}る (check the wind/read the situation)
- {風向|かざむ}きが{悪|わる}い (the wind/mood is unfavorable)

The figurative use (sense 2) is very common and parallels the English expression "which way the wind is blowing."
